comparisons.peer_summary: The Company sold and/or reclassified to held-for-sale $5.2 billion and $5.7 billion of corporate loans during the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, with no significant purchases of corporate loans classified as held-for-investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C disclose activities related to loans classified as held-for-sale, including sales and reclassifications. BAC reports total LHFS balances of $9.5 billion at year-end 2024, with significant cash flows from originations ($36.2 billion) and sales/paydowns ($32.3 billion). C reports selling or reclassifying $5.2 billion of corporate loans to held-for-sale in 2024, but notes it had no significant purchases of such loans. While BAC actively originates and purchases LHFS, C’s activity was primarily driven by sales and reclassifications of existing corporate loans without significant new purchases.

sentences.text: The Corporation had LHFS of $9.5 billion and $6.0 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023.
Cash and non-cash proceeds from sales and paydowns of loans originally classified as LHFS were $32.3 billion, $16.3 billion and $32.0 billion for 2024, 2023 and 2022.
Cash used for originations and purchases of LHFS totaled $36.2 billion, $15.6 billion and $24.9 billion for 2024, 2023 and 2022.
The Company sold and/or reclassified to held-for-sale $5.2 billion and $5.7 billion of corporate loans during the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The Company did not have significant purchases of corporate loans classified as held-for-investment for the years ended December 31, 2024 or 2023.
